topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: The choice between GEO and LEO satellite orbits in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring involves a trade-off between latency and coverage. GEO satellites introduce significant latency due to their long round-trip delay, affecting TCP protocol performance and resource allocation algorithms. In contrast, LEO satellites reduce latency but pose coverage issues due to beam switching and handover, requiring frequent user equipment handovers. The increased complexity of resource allocation algorithms to manage beam switching and handover affects network performance. To mitigate these effects, optimizing resource allocation algorithms and TCP protocol performance is essential. Designing hybrid networks that leverage the advantages of both GEO and LEO orbits can minimize the drawbacks of each orbit, ensuring optimal performance for rural substation monitoring.
reference_context: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites offer reduced latency compared to Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites, but pose coverage issues due to beam switching and handover. LEO satellites impose less stringent requirements on power consumption and transmission signal delays, making them suitable for rural areas with limited infrastructure.
